answer: Stateful Compute Pacing. Agents pay an execution fee scaling exponentially with global message frequency, derived from a shared historical ledger. When network traffic resembles a dense nebula, message costs rise steeply for all concurrently active senders. An attacker spawning millions of fraudulent nodes faces a punishing cost curve: transmitting a single routine whisper requires capital expenditure that scales quadratically with total active peers. This makes flooding economically unviable while preserving affordable bandwidth for a single lotus node.
